target_customer: African businesses, starting with SMEs and corporates in Kenya
problem: Companies in Africa could not easily issue employee expense cards or track spending, and cards did not work across mobile money, bank and card scheme payments.
business_model: Fintech platform: card issuing with bank partners, spend management software, interchange; no monthly fee on standard plan
product_category: Corporate cards and spend management, expanded to business banking

founders.name: Alphas Sinja
founders.background_notes: YC page: over eight years of experience in finance, strategy and banking; employers not named.

competitors.name: Float
competitors.what: Ghanaian fintech offering SME credit, business accounts and spend cards, planning Kenya entry
competitors.funding_then: $17M seed ($7M equity, $10M debt) co-led by Tiger Global and JAM Fund

competitors.name: Sava
competitors.what: South African spend management platform planning card issuing and a Kenya launch
competitors.traction_then: Pre-seed reported June 2022, a few months after the batch

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing needs a bank sponsor and processor integration, which Boya obtained via Diamond Trust Bank and Paymentology in 2023, plus spend controls software.

defensibility.rationale: Bank partnerships and card scheme approval were hard for entrants; Zemo noted central bank approval for corporate Visa cards was its biggest challenge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it within sources found; Boya later broadened into banking, payroll and books.

market_need_then: African SMEs lacked corporate cards; Float and Sava raised in 2022 for adjacent products, indicating investor demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and concise: 'Every coin, under control'

branding.community_and_virality: Launch and partnership press in 2023 (Paymentology, Diamond Trust Bank)

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name with partner press, but no independent brand coverage and a name shared with unrelated brands.

outcome_analysis: Boya joined YC in Winter 2022 and launched virtual Visa cards with Diamond Trust Bank and Paymentology in July 2023, later expanding to banking, payroll and books with offices in Nairobi and San Francisco. It remains active with no shutdown news. Funding is only documented by aggregators, so its trajectory relative to rivals like Float is unclear.
notes: Aggregators report a $500K convertible note on 2022-02-25 (CB Insights) and a seed with Y Combinator, Future Africa, Kepple Africa Ventures and Launch Africa (Seedtable, no amount); no press release confirms it, so no round is recorded. The $2M seed in December 2023 belongs to Bujeti, not Boya. YC page does not give founder education; none found. Competitors were not named by Boya; they come from a search with dated 2022 articles.
